subject: Legal: retention exceptions, subprocessor notice timing & e-sign workflow
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@helixbiotech.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial questions on retention/backups, subprocessors & e-sign path

Olga —

Thanks for the call earlier. Helix legal dug into the draft DPA and flagged three areas we need explicit language on before we can route for CISO sign-off:

1) Backup/DR carve-out: we need to confirm how long data may persist in immutable backups after an account-level delete request or contract termination. Our security team is asking for a finite, auditable retention window and deletion trigger definition.

2) Subprocessors: please confirm the notification cadence for adding new subprocessors. Our policy requires at least 30 days' notice for non-critical additions and expedited notice for security-critical subprocessors. Also want a public list of subprocessors if possible.

3) Cross-border transfers: Helix operates largely in the EU. We need confirmation on the transfer mechanism (SCCs / export controls) and whether Redwood will sign via DocuSign (preferred) or AdobeSign.

Attached is our review spreadsheet and a redline of the DPA (summary notes in column C). Could you confirm whether Redwood can accept a limited backup carve-out (length + scope), publish subprocessors, and proceed via DocuSign envelope?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement would like to finalize by next week if we can get legal tidy.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Senior Counsel, HelixBiotech
samir.patel@helixbiotech.com

Attachments: Helix_DPA_questions.xlsx, Helix_DPA_redline_v2.docx

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@helixbiotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on retention/backups, subprocessors & e-sign path

Samir —

Thanks for the clear list. I attached a short redline from our side (Helix_DPA_redline_v2.docx) and prelim answers below. Happy to hop on a short call but wanted to get these in writing first.

1) Backup / DR retention: Redwood is willing to agree to a limited carve-out for immutable backups strictly for disaster recovery and legal hold. Proposed wording: "Backups: Customer Personal Data included in immutable backup systems may be retained up to 90 days following the date of deletion or account termination solely for the purpose of disaster recovery and legal compliance; such backups will be rotated and sanitized in accordance with Redwood's backup retention policy." This is intended to provide a finite window; we can tighten to 60 days for Helix if that is a firm requirement.

2) Subprocessors: We publish a rolling list of subprocessors on our public trust page (link included in attachments). Standard notice is 30 days for non-critical additions; for security-critical services (e.g., key management, logging), we will provide expedited notice and offer to discuss mitigation measures. We can accept contractual language to provide notice and a right to object within 15 business days for substantial changes.

3) Transfers & e-sign: Redwood uses SCCs for EU transfers and maintains documentation on fallback mechanisms. For execution, DocuSign works fine — we can send a DocuSign envelope (I will populate with the final redline). If Helix requires AdobeSign, let us know; DocuSign is our standard.

Next steps I'm proposing:
- Internal confirmation from Rishi on the backup window and from Marissa on commercial implications (discount/term).
- If agreed, I will send a DocuSign envelope (85012) with the agreed redline and a short signature addendum referencing the backup carve-out and subprocessors publication.

If you need the 60-day alternative, flag it and we'll include both options in the envelope.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Attachment: Helix_DPA_redline_v2.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions on retention/backups, subprocessors & e-sign path

Olga —

Quick notes from infra/compliance: 60 days is safer from a privacy exposure perspective. If we can keep 90 days as a PSB (per-customer exception) only for enterprise accounts with an approved addendum, I'm ok with that commercially.

Also: make sure the delete trigger includes both customer-initiated account deletes AND termination for convenience/expiry. Add a clause that immutable backups containing Customer Data will be logically purged on the earliest of the retention window expiry or confirmed legal hold release.

- Rishi
Director, Platform Security

Olga / Rishi —

Commercial perspective: Helix is a priority account (deal DEAL-9872-RI). We're willing to concede to a 90-day backup carve-out on the DPA provided:
- It's explicitly limited to disaster recovery and legal compliance, with no use for analytics or product development.
- The carve-out is documented in a one-page addendum attached to the DocuSign envelope so sales/procurement can track deviations from standard terms.
- We require publication of the subprocessors list on the trust page and a 10-business-day notice for any security-critical additions (we can offer 30 days for non-critical).

Also: DocuSign envelope is fine. If we attach the addendum and mark the redline approved by execs, we should be good to close this week. I will check available concession budget for this deal and confirm whether we need a pricing approval.

- Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-02T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Final: agreed language for backups, subprocessors & DocuSign envelope (please sign)

Samir / Jane —

Thanks for working through this. Summary of agreed points (please confirm by reply or by signing the DocuSign envelope):

- Backup/DR carve-out: immutable backups containing Customer Personal Data will be retained for up to 90 days following deletion or contract termination, limited strictly to disaster recovery and legal compliance purposes. Per Helix request, the deletion trigger will include customer-initiated deletes and account termination. Redwood will proactively rotate and logically purge backups at the end of the retention window unless a legal hold is in place. (Rishi requested a 60-day alternative; we documented the 60-day option in the addendum as an enterprise-only concession.)

- Subprocessors: Redwood will publish a current list of subprocessors on its trust page and provide 30 days' notice for non-critical additions. For security-critical subprocessors, Redwood will provide expedited notice and a 10-business-day objection window and engage on mitigation.

- Transfers & execution: Redwood will execute SCCs and provide transfer documentation. Execution will be via DocuSign (envelope 85012) — link below. If Helix requires AdobeSign instead, reply and we will accommodate but it will delay signature by 48–72 hours.

DocuSign envelope: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?fid=85012
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/9872

I have attached the redline and the one-page addendum to the envelope. Please sign the DocuSign envelope and we will countersign and return fully executed copies. If you want a short call to walk through the redline, happy to schedule.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Attachments: Helix_DPA_redline_v2.docx, DocuSign_envelope_85012.pdf
